panelTitle: Multi-GPU Split Planner · Tensor & Pipeline Parallel
intro: Pick a 2× or 4× GPU layout and see how model weights and the KV cache above split across the cards, what the interconnect costs you in decode speed, and whether it fits at all. Tensor parallel shards every layer across GPUs and pays an all-reduce on the bus each decode step; pipeline parallel stacks whole layers per GPU and pays a pipeline bubble instead.
tpHint: weights + KV sharded per layer · all-reduce every decode step
ppHint: whole layers per GPU · boundary transfers + bubble
penaltySub: {base} tok/s single-GPU equivalent → {pct}% {bus} sync loss → {effective} tok/s
warnDoesNotFit: {needed} per GPU exceeds {usable} usable on this card ({vram} × 95%). Pick a bigger card, lower the weight quant, or cut context/batch.
warnKvReplicated: Only {kvHeads} KV heads for {n} GPUs in tensor parallel — there is nothing to split, so every card holds a full copy of the KV cache. Pipeline parallel would shard it by layer instead.
warnSingleCardFaster: This whole workload fits on a single {card}. Over PCIe, tensor parallel pays ~10% decode loss to all-reduce every step — one bigger card is both simpler AND faster than two small ones. Only split when no single card can host it.
footnote: Heuristics: PCIe all-reduce ≈ −10% decode for TP (two all-reduce rounds cross the ~64 GB/s bus each step; community-measured deltas cluster at 5–15%), NVLink ≈ −3% (~900 GB/s mostly hides the sync), PP ≈ −2% flat from the pipeline bubble. Usable VRAM = 95% of the card minus ~1.5 GB CUDA/activation overhead per GPU.
